title: Users shift from "tokenmaxxing" to efficiency, and Claude wins paying fans
excerpt: AI users are trading volume for efficiency, Claude is gaining paying consumers, Google's search grip is being tested, and Africa asks who will own the AI infrastructure.

items.t: CNBC reported that OpenAI and Anthropic face a new reality as users move from "tokenmaxxing", using as much AI as possible, to caring about efficiency and cost.

items.h: Claude is winning over paid consumers
items.t: TechCrunch reported that Anthropic's Claude is winning over paying consumers in a market ChatGPT has long owned.

items.h: Google's online dominance shows signs of cracking
items.t: CNBC reported that Google's dominance online is showing signs of cracking in the AI era.

items.h: Who will control Africa's AI infrastructure, and at what cost?
items.t: Al Jazeera examined who will control the data centres and networks behind Africa's AI boom, noting that the physical infrastructure remains uneven.

water.h: Why AI labs are hiring philosophers
water.t: The Economist asked why big AI labs are hiring so many philosophers. Our take: it shows how much of AI work is about judgement and values, not only code.

means.t: Two practical reads this week: a writer who uses ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini daily but never for the same job (MakeUseOf), and a guide to connecting NotebookLM with Claude for research (Tom's Guide). The lesson is to give each tool a job.
Research tip: load your own sources into a tool like NotebookLM so answers come from your documents, with citations you can check.
Fewer, better prompts cost less and work better. Write the full brief once, then reuse it.

prompt: I use AI for these jobs: [list]. Build me a "tool per job" table: job | best tool for it (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, NotebookLM, other) | why | the prompt template I should save. Mark anything you are unsure about so I can check.
